# Fidelity report: does this package reproduce the approved resume?

**Reference resume:** `Approved_Resume_BA` (DOCX and PDF), the latest resume delivered and approved in the chat.
It is not shipped in this package because it contains personal data. Only measurements are recorded here.

## Provenance, stated plainly
- The approved resume was generated by a Node.js script using the `docx` library, then converted with LibreOffice.
- The script files from the earlier chat sessions were **lost in a sandbox reset**. The BA script was **re-created verbatim from the
  chat transcript** and its output was visually checked against the approved render. The DOCX and PDF compared below were produced
  from that re-created script. So "approved output" here means the delivered files, and the Node generator in this package was checked against them.
- The same helper functions produced the other approved resumes (marketing one-pager, two-page master, and so on) with different margins,
  spacing and content. Those were **not** re-verified one by one.

## Test 1: Node generator vs approved DOCX (regenerated from the same content, byte comparison)
| Part | Result |
|---|---|
| word/document.xml | IDENTICAL |
| word/numbering.xml | IDENTICAL |
| word/styles.xml | IDENTICAL |
| word/settings.xml | IDENTICAL |
| word/fontTable.xml | IDENTICAL |
| list of files inside the DOCX | same |

## Test 2: rendered PDF vs approved PDF (plain `soffice --convert-to pdf`, pdftoppm 100 dpi)
| Engine | Pages | pdftotext identical | Max word shift | Differing pixels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Node (`generate.js`) | 1 vs 1 | yes | 0.0 pt | 0 of 967,590 (0.000%) |
| Python (`generate_py.py`, RECONSTRUCTED) | 1 vs 1 | yes | 0.0 pt | 0 of 967,590 (0.000%) |

The Python port needed four fixes before it matched; each one mirrors something docx-js does, and all are commented in `generate_py.py`:
empty document defaults (python-docx's template adds 11 pt and 1.15 line spacing), Word compatibility mode 15 (the template ships 14),
a bare "List Paragraph" style (the template's version adds an indent and contextual spacing), and floored bullet indents (316 twips, not 317).

## Test 3: fonts in the approved PDF
See `approved_pdf_pdffonts.txt` and `../docs/FONTS_AND_RENDERING.md`. Requested: Calibri. Embedded: Carlito (all text) and Liberation Serif (the 11 bullet glyphs only).

## Not proven
- Rendering in Microsoft Word, Google Docs or Pages. Everything was rendered with LibreOffice 24.2.7.2.
- Rendering with real Calibri. It was not installed, so every PDF here embeds Carlito.
- The photo variant is an extension that was **not part of the approved resume**. It was tested only by rendering the fictional sample in LibreOffice.
- The page-fitting ladder in `build.py` is a **codification** of what was previously done by hand, not the original process.
